I immediately told the supplier that the sample was unacceptable and that it would need to be sandblasted and refinished. The supplier then gave me a written promise that if the production parts had the same surface problem, they would remake the entire order for free and cover the shipping costs. They were not a final acceptance of the finished product, as I had not yet received or physically inspected the actual parts. The parts arrived on XX/XX/year>. Every single piece had flaking and peeling powder coating on the corners and edges because no proper surface preparation was done. The defects were only clear after I physically unboxed and handled the parts. I contacted the supplier the same day through XXXX chat and told them the parts had the same issues as the sample. Consumer complaint narrative: I respectfully submit this detailed rebuttal in response to the letters issued by Comenity Bank and Comenity Capital Bank dated XX/XX/XXXX, regarding the XXXX Credit Card and XXXX XXXX XXXX Credit Card accounts. Your response states that you have reviewed the accounts and found no violations of law, that you verified the reporting is accurate, that a fraud investigation was conducted and found no basis to support my fraud claim, and that the accounts were charged off and subsequently sold to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX You further state that you are reporting a XXXX balance owed to you after sale of the accounts. The XXXX account response is reflected in your letter dated XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX-CB-Final Respo . The XXXX account response is reflected in your letter dated XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXXCCB-Final Resp . While I acknowledge receipt of these letters, I do not agree with the conclusions reached, nor do I accept that the reporting of these accounts is accurate or compliant under the circumstances. I. The Core Issue Remains Unresolved The central issue is ownership and authorization. I have consistently maintained that I did not authorize these accounts. I filed identity theft documentation and raised a formal fraud dispute. Your letters state that your Account Protection ( Fraud ) team completed investigations and found no basis to support the fraud claim. However, your responses do not provide : The documentation reviewed The basis for rejecting the fraud claim Any signed application Any identity authentication record Any proof that I personally opened or authorized these accounts A conclusory statement that no basis was found does not resolve a fraud dispute. A meaningful investigation requires documentary evidence, not internal affirmation. II. Reporting a Charged-Off Account That Was Sold Your letters confirm : The XXXX account was charged off XX/XX/XXXX and sold XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX-CB-Final Respo The XXXX account was charged off XX/XX/XXXX and sold XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX-CCB-Final Resp You state that you are reporting a XXXX balance owed to you after sale. However, the issue is not simply balance reporting. The issue is whether : The accounts were validly opened by me. The reporting of charge-off status is accurate if fraud was asserted. The tradelines continue to reflect derogatory status despite sale. If the accounts were opened fraudulently, then the subsequent charge-off and sale do not cure the original defect. A fraudulent account can not become legitimate merely because it was charged off and sold. If I did not authorize the accounts, then : The charge-off is improper. The reporting is inaccurate. The sale transfers a disputed and potentially fraudulent debt. III. Fraud Investigation Was Not Substantiated Your letters state that a fraud investigation was conducted and no basis was found. However, you have not provided : The application used to open the account IP address logs if opened online Identity verification method used Copies of drivers license or documents used to approve the account Signature comparisons Device fingerprinting records Phone recordings ( if applicable ) Without providing these materials, it is impossible to determine whether the fraud investigation was meaningful. A fraud investigation can not be considered complete if the consumer is not shown the evidence used to deny the fraud claim. IV. Sale to XXXX XXXX XXXX Does Not Eliminate Responsibility Both letters state that the accounts were sold to XXXX XXXX XXXX and that XXXX may report under its own name XXXX XXXX-CB-Final Respo XXXX XXXX-CCB-Final Resp. However : Sale of an account does not eliminate responsibility for accurate reporting. A furnisher can not avoid resolving fraud claims by selling the account. If the account was disputed as fraud prior to sale, that dispute follows the account. If the original account opening was unauthorized, then XXXX received a disputed and potentially invalid account. I will address XXXX separately, but Comenity can not simply redirect responsibility. V. XXXX Balance Does Not Cure Derogatory Reporting You state that you are reporting a XXXX balance owed to you. However : The tradeline still reflects charge-off status. The charge-off continues to impact credit scoring. The history of delinquency remains attached. XXXX balance reporting does not eliminate derogatory status. If the account does not belong to me, deletionnot XXXX balance notationis required. VI. Failure to Provide Proof of Authorization If you maintain that the accounts are valid, please provide : Original signed or electronically authenticated application. Timestamped application submission data. Identity verification records. Proof of delivery of cards. Transaction history showing usage attributable to me. Documentation proving I made payments voluntarily. If you can not provide these materials, then there is insufficient basis to continue reporting. VII. Harm Caused by Continued Reporting The continued reporting of these accounts has caused : Credit score suppression Increased lending scrutiny Higher interest exposure Emotional distress Time spent disputing A charge-offeven with XXXX balancehas long-term consequences. VIII. Reasonable Procedures and Accuracy Standards Reporting must meet the standard of maximum possible accuracy. That requires : Verification beyond internal database confirmation Consideration of identity theft documentation Correction where uncertainty exists A generic statement that we verified were reporting correctly is not evidence. IX. What Is Required to Resolve This Matter To fully resolve this dispute, the following must occur : Provide documentary proof of account authorization. If documentation can not be produced, delete both tradelines. Confirm in writing that the accounts will not be reinserted. Ensure XXXX is notified of the dispute and fraud claim. Provide method of verification details. X. Conclusion Your XX/XX/XXXX letters XXXX XXXX-CB-Final Respo XXXX XXXX-CCB-Final Resp do not resolve the fraud dispute. They provide conclusions but not supporting documentation. If the accounts were fraudulently opened, then : The charge-offs are invalid. The sale is improper. The reporting must be deleted. If you possess evidence that I authorized these accounts, please provide it. Absent such proof, continued reporting is unjustified. I respectfully request a renewed review and full documentary substantiation. Until that occurs, this matter remains unresolved.

Consumer complaint narrative: Months ago ( approximately XX/XX/XXXX ), I enrolled in autopay through the Cadillac Financial customer portal and entered my XXXX checking account information for monthly XXXX payments. In XX/XX/XXXX, while reconciling my XXXX account for tax purposes, I discovered that no payments had been withdrawn. I immediately logged into the Cadillac Financial portal and saw that my loan was shown as current and that XXXX payments were marked processed. Cadillac Financial had been marking XXXX consecutive autopay transactions as processed even though no funds were ever withdrawn. I later learned that Cadillac Financial was using an incorrect bank account number ending in XXXX, while my actual account ends in XXXX. The portal did not require reentry of the account number, did not validate the information, and continued to show payments as successfully processed for months. During the week of XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Cadillac Financial to report the issue. The concierge representative stated that Cadillac Financial uses a thirdparty ACH vendor and that if the vendor was not notified on the same day of the error, nothing could be done. I was told by the representative to contact XXXX and request reversals. I explained that I have no ownership or authority over the incorrectly debited account and that XXXX can not act on an account that does not belong to me. I also explained that under ACH rules, Cadillac Financial has responsibilities as the originator. The representative offered no solution other than they could assist in taking a payment. I explained that ( 1 ) the misapplied funds needed to be corrected, and ( 2 ) I had no confidence in the autopay system. The representative stated that internal staff are required to enter account numbers twice, but consumers are not given that safeguard. I asked why that was and received the response " they don't want us messing up ''. When the discussion stalled, I requested a supervisor. I was told I would receive a call back, but no call came. The next day, after significant effort, I reached a supervisor. She repeated that I must contact XXXX and insisted that if the XXXX payments were reversed, I would be reported 120 days past due and charged {$200.00} in late fees. I explained again that I can not reverse payments from an account I do not own. I asked for escalation to her manager. She later stated that her manager, XXXX, agreed that nothing could be done and that I would be reported late. After submitting a negative survey response, I received a call on XX/XX/XXXX from an individual identifying himself as XXXX. He reviewed the file, but largely repeated the same incorrect guidance. I reiterated that Cadillac Financial, as the ACH originator, has obligations and that I was the one who discovered and reported the issue. Despite this, the focus was on arranging payment for the XXXX months of processing errors. Against my better judgment, I agreed to make the payment in good faith. When I asked for his last name, he refused but stated he was a Vice President. He said a supervisor would call me the next day at XXXX XXXX. to obtain payment information. Instead, at XXXX XXXX the next morning, I received a call from a collection 's agent demanding payment. She acknowledged seeing notes on my account, but was not receptive to the situation. That call ended. At XXXX XXXX., a Cadillac Financial supervisor called as scheduled. I provided my account information and authorized full payment. She apologized for the collections call, confirmed the {$200.00} fee would be waived, and stated that the incorrect ACH account would be removed. She also confirmed that the system now showed my account as 120 days past due solely because Cadillac Financial had been marking payments as processed when no funds were withdrawn. Days passed with no followup from XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I called again and left a message. I eventually received a call back from XXXX XXXX, whose last name I obtained from his voicemail. He stated he had spoken with the credit team and that they would send an update to the credit bureaus ensuring no delinquency would be reported. On XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted my regular monthly payment through the Cadillac Financial XXXX. While traveling that weekend, I did not get to check the account until XX/XX/XXXX and discovered that the system had reverted back to the incorrect bank account ending in XXXX. I contacted Cadillac Financial via chat ( transcript available ). The representatives again stated that I must contact XXXX and that changes could only be made the same dayrepeating the same incorrect information. I have made multiple attempts to contact XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX of Customer Experience ) on his cell phone, but he has not returned my calls. At this point, I do not know how to get Cadillac Financial to reverse the incorrect payment because the concierge staff do not understand how to resolve this issue, and the XXXX XXXX will not return calls. I am willing to make the replacement payment, but it will apply to the XXXX period and XXXX create additional issues. I also believe Cadillac Financial does not understand its obligations regarding XXXX authorization, validation, and error correction, even when using a thirdparty vendor. There appears to be a systemic issue with either the Cadillac Financial portal or the handoff to their XXXX vendor. Please let me know if additional information is needed. Thank you for your time and assistance.

Consumer complaint narrative: I enrolled in a debt settlement program with Clarity Debt Resolution around 2024 after being told they would negotiate with my creditors and help reduce my debt. I was instructed to stop paying my creditors and instead make monthly payments into their program ( approximately {$330.00} per month ). Over approximately 20 months, I made consistent payments into the program totaling XXXX XXXX dollars. During this time, my accounts went delinquent, collection activity increased, and my credit score dropped significantly ( from approximately XXXX to the low XXXX ). I was also later sued by a creditor. I later discovered that Clarity had power of attorney and redirected creditor statements and communications away from me, which prevented me from receiving billing statements and managing my accounts directly. One of my active credit accounts was closed and sent to collections after communications were redirected through the program. The client portal showed an accrued balance of approximately {$4900.00} in my account. However, when I cancelled the program, I only received a refund of {$760.00}. I requested a full written accounting of all payments made, fees charged, and how my funds were allocated, but the company did not provide a formal itemized accounting. Instead, I received only verbal explanations and limited portal summaries stating the fees were normal. The companys disclosures acknowledge that participation would likely cause default, increased collection activity, and possible lawsuits, yet I was not adequately informed of the full impact this program would have on my credit, legal exposure, and financial stability. As a result of following their instructions, I suffered severe financial harm, account defaults, legal action from creditors, loss of access to credit, and substantial credit score damage. I believe the fees charged were excessive, the disclosures were insufficient, and the handling of my funds lacks transparency.
